events.text: Eratosthenes estimates Earth’s circumference by comparing the Sun’s angle at noon in Syene and Alexandria.

sources.cite: APS News, This Month in Physics History: Eratosthenes measures the Earth

events.text: Archimedes states the law of the lever and the principle of buoyancy.
Ibn al-Haytham’s Book of Optics argues that vision happens when light enters the eye, and tests claims by controlled experiment.
Copernicus’s On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres puts the Sun, not the Earth, at the center.
Kepler shows that planets move in ellipses and states his three laws of planetary motion.
Galileo’s Sidereus Nuncius reports four moons orbiting Jupiter, seen through his telescope.
Newton’s Principia sets out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
Volta builds the first electric battery, the voltaic pile.
Sadi Carnot analyzes the limits of heat engines, founding thermodynamics.
Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction, the principle behind generators and transformers.
Joule’s experiments and Helmholtz’s 1847 essay establish the conservation of energy.
Maxwell’s “A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field” unites electricity, magnetism and light.

sources.cite: Maxwell, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 155 (1865)

events.text: The Michelson–Morley experiment finds no sign of the “ether” that light was thought to travel through.
Röntgen discovers X-rays.

sources.cite: Nobel Prize in Physics 1901, Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen

events.text: Becquerel discovers radioactivity; Marie and Pierre Curie discover polonium and radium.
J. J. Thomson identifies the electron, the first known subatomic particle.

sources.cite: Nobel Prize in Physics 1906, J. J. Thomson

events.text: Planck proposes that energy is emitted in discrete packets (quanta), starting quantum theory.

sources.cite: Nobel Prize in Physics 1918, Max Planck

events.text: Einstein publishes papers on light quanta (the photoelectric effect), Brownian motion, special relativity and E = mc².

sources.cite: Nobel Prize in Physics 1921, Albert Einstein

events.text: Rutherford shows that an atom’s mass is concentrated in a tiny nucleus.
Einstein completes general relativity: gravity is the curvature of spacetime.
Eclipse expeditions led by Eddington and Dyson measure starlight bending by the Sun, supporting general relativity.

sources.cite: Dyson, Eddington and Davidson, Philosophical Transactions A 220 (1920)

events.text: Heisenberg, Schrödinger, Born, Dirac and others formulate quantum mechanics; Heisenberg states the uncertainty principle (1927).

sources.cite: Nobel Prize in Physics 1932, Werner Heisenberg

events.text: Hubble finds that more distant galaxies recede faster: evidence that the universe is expanding.

sources.cite: Hubble, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 15 (1929)

events.text: Chadwick discovers the neutron.

sources.cite: Nobel Prize in Physics 1935, James Chadwick

events.text: Hahn and Strassmann split uranium; Meitner and Frisch explain it as nuclear fission.

sources.cite: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1944, Otto Hahn

events.text: The first nuclear weapon is tested at Trinity, New Mexico (16 July); atomic bombs destroy Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August.
Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley invent the transistor at Bell Labs, the basis of modern electronics.
Chien-Shiung Wu’s experiment shows that the weak force does not respect mirror symmetry (parity).
Penzias and Wilson detect the cosmic microwave background, the afterglow of the Big Bang.
Jocelyn Bell Burnell discovers the first pulsar, a rapidly spinning neutron star.
Two teams studying distant supernovae find that the universe’s expansion is accelerating.
The ATLAS and CMS experiments at CERN announce the discovery of the Higgs boson (4 July).
LIGO detects gravitational waves from two merging black holes (14 September; announced February 2016).

sources.cite: LIGO and Virgo Collaborations, Physical Review Letters 116 (2016)

events.text: The Event Horizon Telescope publishes the first image of a black hole’s shadow, in the galaxy M87.

sources.cite: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration, Astrophysical Journal Letters 875 (2019)

events.text: The US National Ignition Facility achieves fusion ignition: more energy out of the fuel than the lasers put in (5 December).

sources.cite: US Department of Energy announcement, December 2022

events.text: The Nobel Prize in Physics honors Clarke, Devoret and Martinis for showing quantum tunnelling and quantized energy in an electric circuit large enough to hold in your hand.

people.name: Ibn al-Haytham
people.text: Pioneered experimental optics and the idea that theories must be tested.

people.name: Shen Kuo
people.text: Described the magnetic compass needle and its deviation from true north.

people.name: Emmy Noether
people.text: Proved that every symmetry of nature corresponds to a conserved quantity (Noether’s theorem).

people.name: Lise Meitner
people.text: Co-explained nuclear fission; left out of the 1944 Nobel Prize awarded to her colleague Otto Hahn.

people.name: C. V. Raman
people.text: Discovered how light changes color when it scatters off molecules (the Raman effect); Nobel Prize 1930.

people.name: Satyendra Nath Bose
people.text: Developed the statistics for particles of light, used by Einstein; bosons are named after him.

people.name: Hideki Yukawa
people.text: Predicted the meson to explain the force holding the nucleus together; Japan’s first Nobel laureate (1949).

people.name: Chien-Shiung Wu
people.text: Showed experimentally that parity is violated in the weak interaction.

people.name: Abdus Salam
people.text: Co-developed the unified theory of the electromagnetic and weak forces; Nobel Prize 1979.

people.name: Jocelyn Bell Burnell
people.text: Discovered pulsars as a graduate student in 1967.
